messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1792345600 - streaming token cadence regression detected for service=runtime-inference-2 cluster=us-west-2 group=kv-cache+continuous-batching. 95th pct token latency spike to 4.2s, partial flush events increased x18. Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/alerts/1792345600

MZ (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it. Triage plan: 1) confirm customer impact, 2) check recent deploys/config changes, 3) try immediate mitigations (toggle continuous batching / reduce batch window), 4) escalate if we see errors.

Kevin: Seeing a ton of incomplete streams in the live logs — last_token gaps of 5-10s before the socket flushes. Also KV cache memory spike on host runtime-12. Suspect a race where partial flushes are queued but never emitted when KV paging thrashes.

Fae: I started looking at the commit that changed the continuous-batching heuristics yesterday (deploy 1792309002). There's a change to the flush backoff that could cause indefinite wait if kv-page returns EMPTY and continuous-batch thinks more tokens incoming. Stack snippet: ```
# simplified
if (kv_page.empty() && batching_window_open) {
  wait(backoff_ms *= 2);
  // missing bailout when stream_closed
}
```

Darren: If that logic is right, we can mitigate quickly by disabling the new backoff path and forcing immediate partial flush on EMPTY. Two options: hotpatch runtime config or roll back the deploy. Hotpatch is lower blast.

MZ (oncall): Priority is reduce customer impact. Kevin — can you open a trace for the most affected request ID and capture kv page responses and token timestamps? Maria — can you check the incident channel for any customer tickets?

Kevin: Traces attached (internal link). Example: request rdx-custA-9812 shows token 12 emitted then 7s silence, then final flush of 40 tokens. The KV requests show repeated page requests returning EMPTY and then a delayed page with data; continuous-batcher kept waiting because it expected prefix growth.

Maria: Support Bot shows spikes in 502 and stream timeouts — 7 customers reported degraded interactive latency in the last 10m, one enterprise customer (acme-corp) saw multiple session failures. I've proactively sent the advisory to account team: "Investigating streaming regressions; temporary mitigation in progress."

Fae: Proposed immediate mitigation steps: 1) set runtime flag `streaming.partial_flush_on_empty=true` (forces flush when kv page empty), 2) reduce `continuous_batch.window_ms` from 120 to 20 for affected runtimes, 3) enable fallback routing to model-compat-small for streaming endpoints if latency > 1s.

Darren: I can apply (1) and (2) via infra patch to the runtime config. Command I will run: ```
# apply immediate config to canary and then prod
rdctl runtime config set runtime-inference-2 --key streaming.partial_flush_on_empty --value true --env us-west-2
rdctl runtime config set runtime-inference-2 --key continuous_batch.window_ms --value 20 --env us-west-2
```

MZ (oncall): Do it as a canary first on runtime-12 then roll to runtime-13..16 if stable. Notify here when canary done.

Darren: Canary patch applied to runtime-12 at 1792345840. Restarting worker processes gracefully.

Kevin: Canary metrics: token cadence 95th dropped from 4.2s -> 0.45s on runtime-12, partial flush events back to baseline. No errors on canary. :white_check_mark:

Darren: Rolling to remaining hosts now (runtime-13..16). Patch done by 1792345980.

Support Bot: Notifying affected customers that we have applied a temporary mitigation. Message: "We have applied a configuration change to improve streaming reliability. Some streams may see lower throughput while we stabilize. We will follow up with a root-cause and timeline."

MZ (oncall): Observing overall cluster: 95th token latency down to 0.6s cluster-wide, KV mem pressure reduced ~30%. I'm going to keep monitoring for 30m, then we can plan a code fix and a formal rollback of the heuristic change.

Fae: I'll prepare a patch to the batching logic to add explicit closed-stream bailout and a unit test for the EMPTY -> wait path. Patch branch: fix/streaming-empty-bailout. Proposed changelist: add `if stream_closed(): flush()` and add timeout guard on backoff.

Kevin: One more note: this surfaced where paging latencies are high (S3-backed paging). We should consider making the KV paging layer return a sentinel 'no-more-data' vs EMPTY which the batching logic treats as different. I'll add that to the PR.

MZ (oncall): Handoff: I'm covering oncall for next hour then handing to Kevin at 1802340000 for follow-up. Action items: (1) Fae to open PR and include test, (2) Darren to prepare playbook entry for future hotpatch toggles, (3) Maria to collect affected customer list and timeline, (4) Kevin to add paging sentinel change in the PR.

Darren: I'll also add an emergency knob to the console to flip `partial_flush_on_empty` per-runtime. That made hotpatching quicker.

Maria: Customer update posted to acme-corp and top-10 affected. They're appreciative of the quick mitigation; account team requested postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

Fae: PR opened 1792346400 -> https://git.redwood/changes/12345. Unit tests cover EMPTY -> flush and backoff timeout. Requesting review from SRE and infra.

Kevin: Confirming canary metrics held for 30m. No regression on throughput after patch. Preparing an integration test that emulates delayed KV pages + continuous batching to catch this in CI.

MZ (oncall): Marking this incident as mitigated. We'll keep the runtime flag enabled until the fix is merged + deployed. Postmortem to be scheduled tomorrow; I'll create the page. Thanks everyone for quick response. :pray:

Support Bot: Customers notified. Follow-up tickets created for each customer case.

Darren: Follow-up work: add a monitoring alert for 'partial_flush_rate > 3x baseline' and 'kv-empty-backoff-duration > 1s' so we detect this earlier.

Fae: After deploy, will remove the temporary console knob and rely on config flow. PR merged 1792347600 and staged for canary on next deploy.

MZ (oncall): Handoff complete to Kevin. Last check-in at 1792346800. Thread closed for operational updates; postmortem thread will follow.
